observations: Multiple white plastic IBC (Intermediate Bulk Container) tanks stacked in an outdoor yard.
Tanks are secured with metal pallets and have metal frames.
Red and blue taps are visible on top of some tanks.
The tanks show signs of wear, dirt, and some surface discoloration.
The ground is muddy and littered with debris.
A large dark pipe or tank is visible in the foreground of photo 0 and photo 1.
No brand or model markings are legible on the tanks in any photo.
The seller's text describes the item as a 'chemical tank' for corrosive substances.

claims.claim: A chemical tank is a specialized container built to safely store, mix, or transport corrosive,...
claims.evidence: The photos show IBC tanks, which are standard for chemicals, but the specific suitability for corrosive substances cannot be confirmed from the images alone.

claims.claim: Food grade, used only once for clean water. No crack, no leak, lids complete.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The tanks may have internal leaks or structural damage not visible from the outside.
risks.proof: A video showing the tanks being filled and drained, or a close-up inspection of the seams and base.

risks.risk: The tanks may be contaminated or previously used for hazardous materials.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the tank's interior or a certificate of previous use.

risks.risk: The tanks may be damaged or cracked on the bottom or sides.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the bottom and sides of the tanks.

proof_requests: Close-up photos of the bottom and sides of the tanks to check for cracks or damage.
Photos of the interior of the tanks to check for contamination or residue.
A video showing the tanks being filled and drained to confirm they are leak-free.
Proof of whether the tanks are food-grade or suitable for corrosive chemicals.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
